caseName: The Other Side of the Hotel Door
title: Theo & Lorna

questions.text:
Okay. I have her phone until four. Thank you for doing this.
Three nights this week her phone lit up past midnight, and she flipped it face down like I wasn't standing right there. 😤
Who is Mom talking to that late at night?

Never heard that name in my life. Not once.
A couple months back she came home early in the morning smelling like coffee. Said she'd been 'driving around'. Then made pancakes like nothing happened.
What's the name of the coffee shop where Mom and Rafe met that first morning?
questions.hint: In Messages, find the morning she explains being out early. Then check Photos for something taken that same morning.

questions.text:
Seven in the morning. That's not a coincidence, that's a date. 😳
Then the night she didn't come home at all. She told Dad she was sleeping at Aunt Bea's. Bea lives in Holland, and Mom hates that drive at night.
Where did Mom actually spend the night she said she was at Bea's?
questions.hint: Find the night she told Theo's dad she was staying with her sister. Then go to Settings and check which Wi-Fi networks the phone joined around then.

questions.text:
A tile guy. Okay. He lays tile for a living. Great. Super romantic.
Here's what's been bugging me: her CR-V is still in the driveway on the nights she goes out. Someone picks her up at the corner. I never see the car.
What model is the car Mom's been riding around in?
questions.hint: Check Settings for the cars this phone has paired with, and compare the most recent one with the last night she went out.

questions.text:
A family lawyer. She's actually doing it. She's leaving Dad. 💔
Maddie's fifteen. She cried for a week when Biscuit got sick. I don't know how she survives this.
When is Mom meeting the lawyer in person?
questions.hint: Open Calendar and look ahead for the law firm. Skip the call that already happened.

questions.text:
That's so soon. And Dad's walking around like everything's normal.
When she goes out he just says 'have fun' and goes back to the game. She never tells me where she's going, just 'out'.
What does Mom tell Dad she's doing on her nights out?
questions.hint: In Messages, read her chat with Theo's dad on the nights she goes out. Then compare with her friends' group chat.

questions.text:
She's been on the same paperback for months. The bookmark hasn't moved past chapter three.
Maddie says she caught Mom scrolling some woman's profile in the car, and Mom flipped the phone over super fast.
Mom always told us social media is for teenagers. 🙄
What name is Mom using on social media?
questions.hint: In Instagram, the account you see first isn't the only one. Go to the profile and look for a way to switch accounts.

onboarding.text: Mom's been going out at night. Her phone buzzes after midnight and she flips it face down. Nine nights ago she didn't come home at all. I'm nineteen. I know what that usually means.
onboarding.label: Theo

onboarding.text: This is the woman who drove three hours to campus when I bombed my first chem exam, with a cooler of pancakes. She's my person. Always has been. That's why this is killing me.
onboarding.label: Theo & Lorna

onboarding.text: Lorna Haskell. Forty-six, dental hygienist, up at 5:45 for eighteen years straight. Married to my dad since she was twenty-three. Never posted a thing online in her life. Not the sneaking type. Supposedly.
onboarding.label: Lorna

onboarding.text: Her battery keeps dying, so she left her phone with me to get it fixed. I have it until four. Help me find out who she's been talking to, before Dad does.
onboarding.label: Theo

notes.title: Grandma's buttermilk pancakes
notes.body:
2 cups flour
2 tbsp sugar
2 tsp baking powder
1 tsp baking soda
1/2 tsp salt
2 cups buttermilk
2 eggs
4 tbsp melted butter

Don't overmix. Lumps are fine. Wait for the bubbles before you flip. Medium heat, butter the pan every round.

Theo eats the first two standing at the counter. Every time.
